summary: Infrequent variant activation causes intermittent p99 spikes and 504s
description: Issue summary: Customer QuillWorks is observing intermittent latency regressions and 504 timeouts on a production dedicated deployment. Pattern appears correlated with traffic that briefly routes to an infrequently used model variant (quantized variant) which triggers cold-start behavior and transient p99 spikes. Impact: ~3-5% of requests over the last 48h saw p99 jump from ~120ms to 3-8s and occasional 504s. Customer reports user-facing failures in their document summarization flow. Environment: Dedicated pool (contracted GPUs), us-east primary, routing policy uses variant fallback when capacity/latency targets change. Observed behavior vs expected: Requests occasionally route to the quantized variant that has no warm replicas; cold-start latency plus KV cache warm-up results in long tail latency and occasional gateway timeouts. Expected behavior is that short-lived routing to a slower variant should either (a) route only a small canary with increased timeout or (b) failover to a warm compatible variant rather than send production traffic to an uninitialized replica.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer sends steady low-volume traffic (bursts ~20-30 RPS) to pinned model redwood/gpt-medium-v1 with fallback enabled
2) Trigger simulated load shift by briefly failing a warm replica (we observed in their environment via node drain events)
3) Observe routing decision that directs a fraction of traffic to redwood/gpt-medium-quantized-v1 which has zero warmed replicas
4) Measure p50/p95/p99 and count of 504s during the 30-90s window after activation
comments: 2026-03-10 - QuillWorks (support@quillworks.com): We're seeing intermittent 504s in the summarization endpoint since Tuesday afternoon. No config changes on our side. Request IDs attached in original email.
2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel (Support): Thanks for the report — we're triaging. Can you confirm if you have fallback to quantized variants enabled and whether you pinned model versions?

2026-03-11 - QuillWorks: We do have autoscaling + fallback to quantized variants enabled. We have a pinned primary model but fallback allowed for cost-saving. Unable to reproduce consistently in staging.

2026-03-12 - Marco Chen (SRE): Observed router logs showing short-lived routing to quantized variant followed by instance launches and 504s. Adding engineering to investigate warm-up path and timeout policy.

2026-03-13 - Eng (runtime): Hypothesis: router's capacity check deems primary under pressure and triggers policy to use a variant that has no warm replicas. Launch latency plus KV cache warm-up is longer than gateway timeout. Increasing gateway timeouts temporarily as a mitigation. Planning follow-up to avoid routing to initializing replicas.
2026-03-14 - QuillWorks: After the temporary timeout increase the 504 rate dropped to ~0.5%. Customer requested a permanent fix path and communication to their SREs about expected behavior.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: fallback routing is too aggressive when capacity signals are marginal, and it does not respect 'warm replica' requirement for production traffic.
Checked router decision logs: multiple RouteDecision events where selected_variant was a quantized variant with zero healthy replicas; reason shows fallback_policy(capacity_constraint).
Measured cold-start time: average replica start 2.0-3.5s, KV cache warm-up additional 1.0-3.0s depending on sequence length -> combined tail causes gateway timeouts at 4-6s.
Confirmed the autoscaler drained/terminated a warm primary replica before traffic finished shifting (node drain coincident).
Related past tickets: SUP-4926 (slower variant fallback and coldstarts) shows similar pattern but for a different model family.
resolution: Temporary mitigation applied: increased gateway upstream timeout from 5s to 10s for affected route in us-east; monitoring for error rate and latency.
Workaround documented for customer: disable automatic fallback to quantized variants for critical endpoints or pre-warm quantized replicas during scheduled maintenance windows.

Planned permanent fixes: (1) router policy change to require at least one warm replica before routing >0% production traffic to a variant; (2) prefer warm CPU/GPU-backed compatible variant over launching cold quantized variant when latency SLOs are at risk; (3) improve startup telemetry to tag requests that hit initializing replicas.

Follow-ups: engineer assigned to PR to update router decision logic (linked PR above), SRE to add a protective canary window and tune autoscaler drain policy to avoid simultaneous warm replica termination and routing shifts.
Customer communication: sent summary and next-steps on 2026-03-14; requested re-open if spike recurs after router change rollout.
